Name: Sha Tin Racing, Sat 26 Dec (Boxing Day meeting)
Location: Sha Tin Racecourse, Sha Tin, New Territories, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A day race meeting at Sha Tin Racecourse on the Saturday after Christmas, per a third-party compilation of the HKJC 2026/27 calendar. There is no meeting on 25 or 27 Dec; the nearest Happy Valley night meeting is Wed 23 Dec. Why: Festive-season racing is a long-standing Hong Kong tradition and the most accessible way to see local betting culture; tourists can enter the public stands cheaply.

Name: WinterFest 2026-27: Christmas Town and Central light show (dates TBC)
Location: Statue Square, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: HKTB's annual winter festival; the last edition centred on a 20 m tree, a free Christmas Town with a chalet market at Statue Square Gardens, and a building-light show across eight Central landmarks. Why: The city's signature Christmas photo-op and market, free and walkable from Central/Admiralty.

Name: Hong Kong Ballet: The Nutcracker (A Hong Kong Adventure)
Location: Grand Theatre, Hong Kong Cultural Centre, 10 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Septime Webre's Nutcracker re-set in early 20th-century Hong Kong, danced by Hong Kong Ballet at the Cultural Centre Grand Theatre; 2025 was its fifth year. Why: A uniquely Hong Kong take on the Christmas classic, with Star Ferry and local-landmark scenography.

Name: M+: Myths and Monsters: The Art of Fantasy in Asia
Location: M+, 38 Museum Drive, West Kowloon Cultural District, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Major M+ exhibition on fantasy imagery across Asian art, film, games and manga, in the West Gallery. Why: A headline show at West Kowloon's contemporary museum, running through the whole trip.

Name: M+: Design Ah! Experience the Wonder of Everyday Design
Location: M+, 38 Museum Drive, West Kowloon Cultural District, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Interactive family-friendly design exhibition in the M+ Main Hall Gallery. Why: Hands-on, good for a holiday afternoon with kids or design fans.

Name: M+: Lin Tianmiao and Wang Gongxin: Here and There
Location: M+, 38 Museum Drive, West Kowloon Cultural District, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Two-artist show of Chinese contemporary video and installation art; opens 4 Dec 2026. Why: Fresh opening just before the trip; pairs with Herzog & de Meuron: In Focus (to be ongoing) and the free Xu Bing installation on the Grand Stair (to 3 Jan 2027).

Name: Hong Kong Disneyland: A Disney Christmas (2026 dates TBC)
Location: Hong Kong Disneyland Resort, Lantau Island, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Seasonal Christmas programme with decorations, tree lighting, shows and snow effects. Why: Large, reliably annual festive attraction; a Chinese-language report mentions 20 Nov 2026 to 3 Jan 2027 with a new winter market, but that is not confirmed officially.

Name: A Symphony of Lights: suspended and being replaced
Location: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade, Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Victoria Harbour's nightly 8 pm light and laser show, running since 2004. The 2026-27 budget announced it would end in 2H 2026 and be replaced by light installations at various places and times rather than a nightly show. Why: Don't plan around the nightly show: the government suspended it on 9 Sep 2026 until further notice; a farewell event was being considered and the Peak was floated as a site for the new installations.

Name: Tai Kwun Christmas programme (2026 TBC)
Location: Tai Kwun, 10 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Tai Kwun's heritage compound hosted a 12 m tree, nightly light show, music and a circus show on the Parade Ground last Christmas. Why: A free, atmospheric Central heritage setting for Christmas photos.

Name: Star Ferry (Central to Tsim Sha Tsui)
Location: Central Pier 7 / Tsim Sha Tsui Pier, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The green-and-white harbour ferries that cross Victoria Harbour in about 9 minutes, running roughly 06:30-23:30. Why: The cheapest harbour cruise in the world and a cornerstone of old Hong Kong; the upper deck at dusk gives skyline shots from the water.

Name: Ngong Ping 360 cable car (Crystal Cabin)
Location: Ngong Ping 360 Tung Chung Terminal, 11 Mei Tung Street, Tung Chung, Lantau Island, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Lantau cable car from Tung Chung to Ngong Ping with optional glass-floor Crystal Cabins, near Big Buddha. Why: Spectacular sea and mountain views, combined with Po Lin Monastery and Tai O.

Name: Duk Ling aged junk harbour sail
Location: Boarding at Tsim Sha Tsui East landing on the Avenue of Stars promenade, Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui (Klook/KKday); Discover HK also lists Kowloon Public Pier 3. Confirm on ticket., Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A restored wooden junk with red sails offering short Victoria Harbour trips. Why: Rare chance to see the skyline from a traditional junk.

Name: Tai O sampan ride and pink dolphin watching
Location: Tai O, Lantau Island, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Short sampan rides through Tai O's stilt-house channels, or dedicated Hong Kong DolphinWatch trips for Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins. Why: Fishing-village stilt houses and a chance at Hong Kong's wild pink dolphins.

Name: Neon sign workshop (Amazing Neon HK)
Location: Flat 13, 18/F, Laurels Industrial Centre, 32 Tai Yau Street, San Po Kong, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 1.5-hour class bending a single-colour neon sign, from a studio in San Po Kong. Why: Neon is vanishing in HK; make your own piece.

Name: Glocal Mahjong tile colouring workshop (PMQ)
Location: PMQ, 35 Aberdeen Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 1.5-hour guided workshop colouring engraved mahjong tiles at PMQ, for 2-4 guests. Why: Hands-on mahjong craft at the PMQ design hub.

Name: Hong Kong-style egg tart and mooncake class (Bake Your Own)
Location: Shop 407, 4/F, Mira Place 1, 132 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Two-hour private baking class making egg tarts and custard mooncakes, at Mira Place 1, TST. Why: Learn a Hong Kong staple.

Name: Xiqu Centre Cantonese opera
Location: Xiqu Centre, 88 Austin Road West, West Kowloon, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: West Kowloon's Chinese opera theatre with the Grand Theatre and the Tea House Theatre showcasing daily excerpts. Why: Best place to see Cantonese opera.

Name: Ding Ding tram and TramOramic open-top tour
Location: Tram line along Des Voeux Road / Hennessy Road / King's Road, Kennedy Town to Shau Kei Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The 1904 double-deck tram line along the north shore of Hong Kong Island, plus a one-hour open-top sightseeing tour from Western Market or Causeway Bay. Why: A living heritage vehicle; the front upper-deck seat gives street-level views of tong lau density. Fare rose to HK$3.30 in 2026.

Name: Wong Tai Sin fortune-telling (kau chim)
Location: Wong Tai Sin Temple, 2 Chuk Yuen Village, Wong Tai Sin, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Shake a canister of numbered sticks (kau chim) until one falls, then have a fortune-teller in the temple's arcade interpret it; some speak English. Why: Rooted Cantonese folk practice at the city's busiest temple; free to try yourself with the temple's stick lookup, readings cost extra (reported from about HK$100).

Name: Morning tai chi at Victoria Park
Location: Victoria Park, Causeway Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Informal early-morning tai chi groups practise in the park; visitors are often welcome to watch or join. The Hong Kong Tourism Board has also run free beginner classes (dates not found). Why: Authentic local ritual at no cost, easy before a Causeway Bay breakfast. Sunrise is about 07:00.

Name: Tai Pan Reflexology Parlour
Location: B/F, 83 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: 1940s-styled parlour doing foot reflexology with a leg soak in vintage barber-style chairs; a 2026 guide lists HK$400-700. Why: A themed take on the Cantonese foot-massage habit near Jordan; not a gritty local shop, so ask Chinese-language sources for neighbourhood parlours.

Name: Villain hitting under the Canal Road Flyover
Location: Under the Canal Road Flyover (Goose Neck Bridge), Canal Road West / Hennessy Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A folk ritual in which a practitioner (often an older woman) beats a paper figure of your enemy with a shoe, burns paper offerings and chants to remove bad luck. Booths line the underpass of the flyover. Why: The best-known 'villain beating' site in Hong Kong, a Cantonese tradition (pronounced 'da siu yan') that peaks on Jingzhe (early March) but runs year-round; Causeway Bay's flyover is the site most visitors know.

Name: Aberdeen Harbour sampan ride
Location: Aberdeen Promenade sampan pier, Aberdeen Praya Road, Aberdeen, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A 20-30 minute ride on a motorised wooden sampan around Aberdeen Typhoon Shelter, passing fishing junks, houseboats and the old floating-village waterfront, with the new towers behind. Why: A glimpse of Hong Kong's fishing-boat community that once lived afloat; note the Jumbo Floating Restaurant is gone, so rides now mainly tour the shelter.

Name: Aqua Luna red-sail junk cruise
Location: Tsim Sha Tsui Public Pier No. 1 (Cultural Centre) and Central Pier 9, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A red-sailed Chinese-style junk that cruises Victoria Harbour between Central Pier 9 and TST Pier 1, with themed day and evening cruises; a free drink is included. Dinner and festive cruises run in December. Why: The photogenic red sails are a Hong Kong postcard image; a harbour cruise on the skyline gives a different perspective from the Star Ferry.

Name: Happy Valley Racecourse (Wednesday night racing)
Location: Happy Valley Racecourse, 2 Sports Road, Happy Valley, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The city's inner-urban racecourse, where Wednesday night meetings turn the track into a lit stadium among apartment towers. Visitors can buy a tourist entrance badge to the public stands; the HKJC Racing Museum is on site. Why: A defining Hong Kong ritual of betting and beer under floodlights; the 2026/27 season has 38 Happy Valley night meetings.
